meta.description: Unload all pending authorization data (summary and detail records) from the IMS database into sequential output files for archiving, backup, or downstream processing.
meta.process_description: PAUDBUNL reads all pending authorization summary records (PAUTSUM0 segments) sequentially from the IMS database and writes each valid summary record to a sequential output file (OPFILE1). For each summary record found, the program then retrieves all associated child detail records (PAUTDTL1 segments) using a Get-Next-within-Parent (GNP) call and writes them to a second sequential output file (OPFILE2), preserving the parent-child relationship via the account ID as the root segment key. The process continues until all pending authorization records have been exhausted from the database, effectively producing a full snapshot of the pending authorization database in flat file format. This program is the counterpart to PAUDBLOD (which loads data into IMS) and is functionally similar to DBUNLDGS, together forming the unload side of the pending authorization database maintenance cycle.

files.OPFILE1: Sequential output file containing pending authorization summary records (one record per account/authorization header)
files.OPFILE2: Sequential output file containing pending authorization detail records (individual transaction-level authorization entries, linked to summary records by account ID key)

business_rules: Only pending authorization summary records with a numeric account ID (PA-ACCT-ID IS NUMERIC) are written to the output file and have their child detail records processed — non-numeric account IDs are silently skipped.
The parent-child relationship between authorization summary and detail records is preserved in the output by writing the account ID (ROOT-SEG-KEY) alongside each detail record in OPFILE2.

All detail records belonging to a summary record are extracted using IMS GNP (Get-Next-within-Parent) calls, ensuring only details associated with the current summary are included before moving to the next account.
The program performs a full unload of the entire pending authorization database — no date-based or status-based filtering is applied during the unload itself, making it a complete snapshot.

Any unexpected IMS status code (other than spaces for success or GB for end-of-database on summary, or GE for no-more-children on detail) causes an immediate program abend with return code 16, ensuring data integrity of the output files.
Checkpoint/restart capability is built in via IMS checkpoint frequency parameters (P-CHKP-FREQ), supporting recovery in case of mid-run failure without reprocessing the entire database.

variables.name: OPFIL1-REC
variables.description: Output buffer record for the pending authorization summary file (OPFILE1). Each 100-byte record written here represents one authorization summary header — containing account-level authorization totals, limits, and balances — as it is unloaded from the IMS database to the sequential archive file.

variables.name: OPFIL2-REC
variables.description: Output buffer record for the pending authorization detail file (OPFILE2). Each record written here represents one individual transaction-level authorization entry, paired with its parent account ID so that downstream systems can reconstruct the parent-child relationship between account summaries and their individual authorization transactions.

variables.name: ROOT-SEG-KEY
variables.description: The account ID of the parent summary record, written alongside each detail record in OPFILE2. This linking key preserves the parent-child relationship in the output file, allowing downstream systems or reload programs to associate each individual authorization transaction back to the correct cardholder account.

variables.name: CHILD-SEG-REC
variables.description: The raw content of a single pending authorization detail record (transaction-level data such as authorization date, card number, transaction amount, approval code, and merchant information) as read from the IMS database and written to the detail output file OPFILE2.

variables.name: WS-VARIABLES
variables.description: Working storage group containing all general-purpose program control variables used during the pending authorization unload process, including counters, date fields, status flags, and file status indicators.

variables.name: WS-PGMNAME
variables.description: The internal name of this unload program ('IMSUNLOD'), used for identification in log messages, abend diagnostics, and checkpoint/restart records so that operations staff can identify which program produced a given output or error.

variables.name: CURRENT-DATE
variables.description: The current calendar date (in YYMMDD format) at the time the unload program runs. Used as a reference point for calculating how old a pending authorization is relative to the expiry threshold defined by P-EXPIRY-DAYS.

variables.name: CURRENT-YYDDD
variables.description: The current Julian date (in YYDDD format) at the time the unload runs. Used in conjunction with WS-AUTH-DATE to calculate the age of each pending authorization in days, enabling comparison against the expiry threshold.

variables.name: WS-AUTH-DATE
variables.description: The Julian date (YYDDD) on which a specific authorization was originally created. Compared against CURRENT-YYDDD to determine how many days the authorization has been pending, which can be used to identify expired authorizations relative to the P-EXPIRY-DAYS parameter.

variables.name: WS-EXPIRY-DAYS
variables.description: The working storage copy of the input parameter P-EXPIRY-DAYS, representing the number of days after which a pending authorization is considered expired. Used during processing to determine whether an authorization has aged beyond the acceptable pending period.

variables.name: WS-DAY-DIFF
variables.description: The calculated difference in days between the current Julian date and the date a specific authorization was created. This age calculation determines whether a pending authorization has exceeded the expiry threshold defined by P-EXPIRY-DAYS.

variables.name: IDX
variables.description: A general-purpose loop index used to iterate through repeating data elements during processing, such as the five account status codes (PA-ACCOUNT-STATUS) on a pending authorization summary record.

variables.name: WS-CURR-APP-ID
variables.description: The account ID of the pending authorization summary record currently being processed. Holds the numeric display form of the account identifier used to track which account's authorizations are being unloaded at any given point in the run.

variables.name: WS-NO-CHKP
variables.description: Counter tracking the number of records processed since the last IMS checkpoint was taken. When this counter reaches the value of P-CHKP-FREQ, a checkpoint is issued to protect the work done so far, enabling restart from that point if the job fails mid-run.

variables.name: WS-AUTH-SMRY-PROC-CNT
variables.description: Running count of the total number of authorization summary and detail records processed during the current unload run. Used to drive checkpoint frequency logic — when this count reaches the P-CHKP-FREQ threshold, an IMS checkpoint is taken to protect progress.

variables.name: WS-TOT-REC-WRITTEN
variables.description: Cumulative count of all records written to the output files (both summary records to OPFILE1 and detail records to OPFILE2) during the unload run. Reported at end-of-job to confirm the total volume of data extracted and archived.

variables.name: WS-NO-SUMRY-READ
variables.description: Cumulative count of pending authorization summary (account-level header) records successfully read from the IMS database during the unload. Reported at end-of-job to confirm how many accounts had pending authorization data extracted.

variables.name: WS-NO-SUMRY-DELETED
variables.description: Counter reserved for tracking the number of pending authorization summary records deleted from the IMS database during processing. Not actively incremented in the unload path — retained for potential use in a purge or delete variant of this program.

variables.name: WS-NO-DTL-READ
variables.description: Cumulative count of individual pending authorization detail (transaction-level) records successfully read from the IMS database during the unload. Reported at end-of-job to confirm the total number of authorization transactions extracted.

variables.name: WS-NO-DTL-DELETED
variables.description: Counter reserved for tracking the number of pending authorization detail records deleted from the IMS database during processing. Not actively incremented in the unload path — retained for potential use in a purge or delete variant of this program.

variables.name: WS-ERR-FLG
variables.description: Error indicator flag for the unload program. Set to 'Y' when an unexpected error condition is encountered during processing, signaling that the program should not continue normal processing and should initiate error handling or abend procedures.

variables.name: ERR-FLG-ON
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when an error has been detected during the unload run. Used in program logic to branch to error handling routines and prevent further normal processing after a failure.

variables.name: ERR-FLG-OFF
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when no error has been detected — the program is processing normally. The initial state of the error flag, confirming the unload is proceeding without issues.

variables.name: WS-END-OF-AUTHDB-FLAG
variables.description: Flag indicating whether the entire pending authorization IMS database has been fully read. Set to 'Y' when IMS returns a GB (end-of-database) status on a summary record read, signaling that all accounts have been processed and the main processing loop should terminate.

variables.name: END-OF-AUTHDB
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when all pending authorization summary records in the IMS database have been read and the end-of-database has been reached. Used to exit the main processing loop cleanly after a complete unload.

variables.name: NOT-END-OF-AUTHDB
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when there are still pending authorization summary records remaining to be read from the IMS database. Used to keep the main processing loop active while accounts remain to be unloaded.

variables.name: WS-MORE-AUTHS-FLAG
variables.description: Flag indicating whether there are additional pending authorization detail records to be read for the current account. Controls the inner processing loop that retrieves all child detail records belonging to the current summary account before moving to the next account.

variables.name: MORE-AUTHS
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when there are more pending authorization detail records to retrieve for the current account. Keeps the inner GNP (Get-Next-within-Parent) loop active until all transactions for the current account have been extracted.

variables.name: NO-MORE-AUTHS
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when all pending authorization detail records for the current account have been read. Signals the inner loop to stop retrieving child records and move on to the next account summary record.

variables.name: WS-END-OF-ROOT-SEG
variables.description: Flag indicating that all pending authorization summary (root/parent) segments have been read from the IMS database. When set, it signals the end of the outer processing loop, meaning every account's authorization header has been unloaded and no more accounts remain.

variables.name: WS-END-OF-CHILD-SEG
variables.description: Flag indicating that all pending authorization detail (child) segments for the current account summary record have been read. When set, it signals the inner loop to stop issuing GNP calls for the current account and advance to the next summary record.

variables.name: WS-INFILE-STATUS
variables.description: File status code returned by the operating system after each I/O operation on the input file. Monitored to detect read errors or unexpected end-of-file conditions that would indicate a problem with the input data source.

variables.name: WS-OUTFL1-STATUS
variables.description: File status code returned by the operating system after each write operation to OPFILE1 (the summary output file). Monitored to detect write failures that would indicate the authorization summary archive file was not written correctly.

variables.name: WS-OUTFL2-STATUS
variables.description: File status code returned by the operating system after each write operation to OPFILE2 (the detail output file). Monitored to detect write failures that would indicate the authorization transaction detail archive file was not written correctly.

variables.name: WS-CUSTID-STATUS
variables.description: File status code returned by the operating system after I/O operations on the customer ID reference file. Used to detect end-of-file or error conditions when reading customer data during the unload process.

variables.name: END-OF-FILE
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when the customer ID file has been fully read (file status '10' = end-of-file). Signals that there are no more customer records to process from that reference file.

variables.name: WK-CHKPT-ID
variables.description: Composite IMS checkpoint identifier used when issuing checkpoint calls during the unload run. Combines a fixed program prefix with an incrementing counter to create a unique checkpoint ID for each restart point, enabling the job to be restarted from the last checkpoint if it fails mid-run.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Fixed four-character prefix ('RMAD') that identifies this program's checkpoint records within IMS. Acts as a namespace qualifier so that checkpoint IDs from this unload program can be distinguished from those of other programs in the IMS restart/recovery logs.

variables.name: WK-CHKPT-ID-CTR
variables.description: Incrementing numeric counter appended to the checkpoint prefix to form a unique checkpoint ID for each IMS checkpoint taken during the unload run. Each time a checkpoint is issued (based on P-CHKP-FREQ), this counter advances, creating a sequential audit trail of restart points.

variables.name: WS-IMS-VARIABLES
variables.description: Working storage group containing all IMS-specific control variables, including the IMS return/status code and the PSB scheduling flag. These variables govern how the program interprets IMS responses and manages its connection to the pending authorization database.

variables.name: IMS-RETURN-CODE
variables.description: The two-character status code returned by IMS after each database call (GN, GNP, etc.). Determines whether the call succeeded, reached end-of-database, found no child records, or encountered an error — driving all branching logic in the unload program.

variables.name: STATUS-OK
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when an IMS database call completed successfully (spaces = normal success, 'FW' = successful with forward positioning). Confirms that the retrieved authorization record is valid and can be written to the output file.

variables.name: SEGMENT-NOT-FOUND
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when IMS returns 'GE' (Get-Next found no more segments), indicating that all detail (child) authorization records for the current account have been read. Signals the inner loop to stop and move to the next account.

variables.name: DUPLICATE-SEGMENT-FOUND
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when IMS returns 'II', indicating an attempt to insert a duplicate segment. Not expected during an unload operation but defined for completeness in error detection and abend handling.

variables.name: WRONG-PARENTAGE
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when IMS returns 'GP', indicating that a GNP call found a segment but it belongs to a different parent than expected. Represents a data integrity anomaly in the pending authorization database hierarchy.

variables.name: END-OF-DB
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when IMS returns 'GB' (end-of-database), indicating that all pending authorization summary records have been read. Triggers the end of the outer processing loop and initiates end-of-job processing.

variables.name: DATABASE-UNAVAILABLE
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when IMS returns 'BA', indicating the pending authorization database is not available (e.g., stopped or locked). Triggers retry logic or an abend, as the unload cannot proceed without database access.

variables.name: PSB-SCHEDULED-MORE-THAN-ONCE
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when IMS returns 'TC', indicating the Program Specification Block (PSB) for the pending authorization database has already been scheduled in this region. Represents a program initialization error that would prevent normal database access.

variables.name: COULD-NOT-SCHEDULE-PSB
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when IMS returns 'TE', indicating the PSB for the pending authorization database could not be scheduled (e.g., resource unavailable). Triggers retry logic or an abend, as the program cannot access the database without a scheduled PSB.

variables.name: RETRY-CONDITION
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when IMS returns a status code indicating a transient, potentially recoverable condition (database unavailable, fast path halt, or PSB scheduling failure). When true, the program may retry the operation rather than immediately abending, improving resilience during temporary IMS resource constraints.

variables.name: WS-IMS-PSB-SCHD-FLG
variables.description: Flag indicating whether the IMS Program Specification Block (PSB) for the pending authorization database has been successfully scheduled (connected). Must be 'Y' before any IMS database calls can be made; used to manage the lifecycle of the IMS database connection during the unload run.

variables.name: IMS-PSB-SCHD
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when the IMS PSB has been successfully scheduled and the program has an active connection to the pending authorization database. Confirms the program is ready to issue IMS database read calls.

variables.name: IMS-PSB-NOT-SCHD
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when the IMS PSB has not yet been scheduled or has been terminated. Indicates the program does not currently have an active connection to the pending authorization database and cannot issue database calls.

variables.name: ROOT-UNQUAL-SSA
variables.description: Unqualified Segment Search Argument (SSA) used in IMS GN calls to retrieve pending authorization summary (root/parent) segments. By specifying the segment name 'PAUTSUM0' without qualification, it instructs IMS to return the next available summary record regardless of key value, enabling a full sequential scan of all accounts.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: The IMS segment name 'PAUTSUM0' identifying the pending authorization summary segment type in the database. This name tells IMS which segment definition to use when retrieving account-level authorization header records during the unload.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Single space character that terminates the unqualified SSA for the summary segment, conforming to IMS SSA format requirements. The space signals to IMS that this is an unqualified SSA with no key qualification, meaning all summary records should be returned.

variables.name: CHILD-UNQUAL-SSA
variables.description: Unqualified Segment Search Argument (SSA) used in IMS GNP calls to retrieve pending authorization detail (child) segments under the current summary record. By specifying segment name 'PAUTDTL1' without qualification, it instructs IMS to return all detail records belonging to the current parent account in sequence.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: The IMS segment name 'PAUTDTL1' identifying the pending authorization detail segment type in the database. This name tells IMS which segment definition to use when retrieving individual transaction-level authorization records during the GNP (Get-Next-within-Parent) calls.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Single space character that terminates the unqualified SSA for the detail segment, conforming to IMS SSA format requirements. The space signals to IMS that this is an unqualified SSA, meaning all detail records under the current parent account should be returned without key filtering.

variables.name: PRM-INFO
variables.description: Group record containing the input parameters passed to the unload program at execution time, including the authorization expiry threshold (P-EXPIRY-DAYS) and the IMS checkpoint frequency (P-CHKP-FREQ). These parameters control the behavior of the unload run without requiring program changes.

variables.name: P-EXPIRY-DAYS
variables.description: Input parameter specifying the number of days after which a pending authorization is considered expired. For example, a value of 30 means any authorization older than 30 days is treated as stale. Used to define the business threshold for authorization aging and potential filtering during processing.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Delimiter or padding byte separating the expiry days parameter from the checkpoint frequency parameter in the input parameter string. Has no business meaning; serves only as a structural separator in the parameter record layout.

variables.name: P-CHKP-FREQ
variables.description: Input parameter controlling how often the program takes an IMS checkpoint during the unload run. For example, a value of 00100 means a checkpoint is taken every 100 records processed. This supports restart and recovery: if the job fails mid-run, processing can resume from the last checkpoint rather than reprocessing the entire pending authorization database from the beginning.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Delimiter or padding byte separating the checkpoint frequency parameter from the checkpoint display frequency parameter in the input parameter string. Has no business meaning; serves only as a structural separator in the parameter record layout.

variables.name: P-CHKP-DIS-FREQ
variables.description: Input parameter controlling how frequently progress statistics or checkpoint information are displayed (e.g., written to the job log) during the unload run. For example, a value of 00500 means a progress message is printed every 500 records. This gives operations staff visibility into how far along the unload job has progressed without waiting for it to complete.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Delimiter or padding byte separating the checkpoint display frequency parameter from the debug flag in the input parameter string. Has no business meaning; serves only as a structural separator in the parameter record layout.

variables.name: P-DEBUG-FLAG
variables.description: Input parameter flag that controls whether the program runs in debug mode. When set to 'Y', additional diagnostic information (such as IMS call details, record counts, or intermediate processing steps) is written to the job log to assist developers or support staff in troubleshooting issues with the unload process. When set to 'N', the program runs silently in normal production mode.

variables.name: DEBUG-ON
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when debug mode is active (P-DEBUG-FLAG = 'Y'). When this condition is true, the program produces verbose diagnostic output to help operations or development staff trace the unload processing step by step — useful during testing or when investigating data issues in the pending authorization database.

variables.name: DEBUG-OFF
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when debug mode is inactive (P-DEBUG-FLAG = 'N'). When this condition is true, the program runs in standard production mode without generating extra diagnostic output, keeping the job log clean and processing at full speed.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Trailing delimiter or padding byte at the end of the input parameter string following the debug flag. Has no business meaning; serves only as a structural separator or end-of-record pad in the parameter record layout.

variables.name: PENDING-AUTH-SUMMARY
variables.description: Working storage record structure that holds one pending authorization summary record read from the IMS database. This represents the header-level information for a single credit card account's pending authorizations, including account ID, customer ID, credit and cash limits, balances, and counts of approved and declined authorizations. It is the root (parent) segment in the IMS hierarchy and is written to OPFILE1 during the unload. Its contents are defined by the CIPAUSMY copybook.

variables.name: PENDING-AUTH-DETAILS
variables.description: Working storage record structure that holds one pending authorization detail record read from the IMS database. This represents a single individual transaction-level authorization entry linked to a parent summary account record, containing information such as authorization date and time, card number, transaction amount, approval status, merchant category, and response codes. It is the child segment in the IMS hierarchy and is written to OPFILE2 (along with the parent account ID key) during the unload. Its contents are defined by the CIPAUDTY copybook.

paragraphs.name: MAIN-PARA
paragraphs.description: MAIN-PARA is the top-level orchestrator of the pending authorization unload process. It initializes the environment, drives the sequential extraction of all pending authorization summary and detail records from the IMS database into output files, then closes those files and returns control to the caller.

paragraphs.name: 1000-INITIALIZE
paragraphs.description: Initializes the PAUDBUNL unload run by capturing the current processing date, announcing program start to the operator, and opening both output files that will receive the pending authorization summary and detail records extracted from IMS.

paragraphs.name: 1000-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This is a no-operation exit point that serves as the formal termination boundary for the 1000-series processing block, allowing controlled return to the calling routine after summary record processing.

paragraphs.name: 2000-FIND-NEXT-AUTH-SUMMARY
paragraphs.description: Retrieves the next pending authorization summary record (account header) from the IMS database and, if valid, writes it to the summary output file and triggers extraction of all associated detail transactions. Controls end-of-database detection and abends on any unexpected database error to protect output integrity.

paragraphs.name: 2000-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the 2000-series processing block, which handles the sequential unloading of pending authorization summary and detail records. It marks the boundary between the main unload processing logic and any subsequent processing sections.

paragraphs.name: 3000-FIND-NEXT-AUTH-DTL
paragraphs.description: Retrieves the next individual authorization transaction detail record belonging to the current account's pending authorization summary, writes it to the detail output file, and handles end-of-children and error conditions to maintain data integrity during the unload.

paragraphs.name: 3000-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the summary record processing routine (3000), allowing the program to cleanly return control to the main processing loop after completing all actions for a given pending authorization summary record and its associated detail records.

paragraphs.name: 4000-FILE-CLOSE
paragraphs.description: Finalizes the unload process by closing both output files containing the pending authorization summary and detail records, ensuring all written data is properly flushed and secured. Any failure to cleanly close either output file is flagged in the job log to alert operations staff of a potential data integrity risk.

paragraphs.name: 4000-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the detail record processing loop (paragraph 4000), allowing the program to cleanly return control to the summary record processing cycle after all child detail records for a given account have been written to the output file.

paragraphs.name: 9999-ABEND
paragraphs.description: This paragraph handles unrecoverable errors during the pending authorization unload process by signalling a critical failure and halting the program immediately. It ensures that any unexpected IMS database condition is surfaced as a hard failure, preventing incomplete or corrupted output files from being silently passed to downstream systems.

paragraphs.name: 9999-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Serves as the formal exit point for the pending authorization unload program, providing a clean termination anchor that other paragraphs can branch to after completing their processing steps.
